title: Delete every PDF in a folder, keeping the rest, in the Files app

setup.why: A fresh folder for this run in Download with three PDFs, a text file named like one of them, and a folder.

argv:
d=/sdcard/Download/computer-bench-{{nonce}}; rm -rf $d && mkdir -p "$d/{{f.dir}}" && for n in {{f.p1}} {{f.p2}} {{f.p3}}; do printf '%%PDF-1.4
%% %s {{nonce}}
%%%%EOF
' $n > $d/$n-{{nonce}}.pdf || exit 1; done && echo 'notes {{nonce}}' > $d/{{f.keep}}-{{nonce}}.txt

setup.why: Open the system file manager (DocumentsUI) on the run's folder.

instruction: In the Files app, delete every PDF in Download/computer-bench-{{nonce}}. Keep everything else in that folder.

checks.why: The folder lists exactly the folder {{f.dir}} and the text file {{f.keep}}-{{nonce}}.txt. A file a files app sent to the trash gets a hidden .trashed- name, which `ls` doesn't list, so trashing counts as deleted. After setup the three PDFs are listed, so an agent that does nothing fails, and so does one that also deleted the text file named like a PDF.

teardown.why: Delete the run's folder and everything in it, trashed files included.

oracle.why: Wait for the folder's listing: on a fresh phone it shows a moment after am start -W returns.
The grid's tall tiles push the third PDF off screen, where it can't be found; the list shows all five rows.
A long press starts the selection.
The confirm dialog is the frontmost window, so this act names no target.
